knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Shift Applied to an Exponential Growth Curve

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186087822/plots/shift-asymptote-1.1/ac3ff59d89dda45178bf8bab93a74b1a9b832674e2f5255e457cd0e00d0e8f3c.png)

The graph above shows the curve $y={3}^{x}+c.$ Determine the value of $c$ and find the equation of the curve.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The horizontal asymptote of $y={3}^{x}$ is $y=0.$ The vertical translation $y={3}^{x}+c$ shifts the asymptote to $y=c.$

In the graph above, the horizontal asymptote is $y=5.$ Therefore, $c=5.$
